summary:
Earth Jukebox – Hear the Planet is an interactive, accessibility-focused platform that transforms NASA's Earth Science visualizations into dynamic soundscapes. It addresses the challenge of making complex environmental information accessible beyond visual interpretation, particularly for blind and low-vision audiences.

Using computer vision and creative audio synthesis, Earth Jukebox translates visual characteristics such as brightness, color distribution, spatial patterns and changes between frames into musical elements including pitch, rhythm, volume and sound textures.

Users can explore Earth visualizations, experience their auditory interpretations and discover environmental patterns through a new sensory dimension. The platform aims to combine scientific exploration, accessibility and creative technology into one engaging experience.

Our vision is simple: everyone should have the opportunity to experience the changing story of our planet, even without seeing it.
details:
Earth Jukebox – Hear the Planet

1. What does our project do?

Earth Jukebox is an interactive web-based platform that transforms NASA Earth Science visualizations into soundscapes. It explores a simple but powerful idea: what if people could hear the changing planet instead of only seeing it?

NASA produces incredible visualizations of ocean currents, atmospheric changes, global temperatures, carbon dioxide concentrations, forest coverage and other Earth systems. However, presenting this information primarily through visuals can create accessibility barriers, particularly for people who are blind or have low vision.

Earth Jukebox introduces an additional sensory experience by translating visual information into dynamic audio.

2. How does it work?

The platform connects Earth imagery with a real-time sonification engine. Users can explore NASA visualization resources or provide compatible images and videos.

The system analyses visual characteristics such as brightness, colour distribution, pixel intensity and changes between frames. These characteristics are mapped to musical parameters:

  • Brightness influences sound intensity and volume.
  • Colour variations influence pitch and musical tones.
  • Changes between frames influence rhythm and sound activity.
  • Spatial distribution influences stereo positioning.
  • Visual variation influences sound texture.

Using these mappings, the application generates evolving soundscapes that allow users to explore patterns through listening.

3. Technology used

We developed Earth Jukebox using a combination of web technologies and audio processing:

  • Python and FastAPI for the backend.
  • HTML, CSS and JavaScript for the interactive interface.
  • JavaScript Web Audio API for sound generation.
  • Computer vision and pixel-level image analysis for extracting visual features.
  • NASA Scientific Visualization Studio (SVS) resources for Earth science visualizations.

The application also includes audio controls and visualization features to make the listening experience interactive.

4. What makes it different?

Our approach combines scientific visualization with creative audio design. Instead of simply attaching background music to NASA videos, Earth Jukebox establishes a relationship between visual characteristics and generated sound.

The objective is to make the audio meaningful, responsive and enjoyable while preserving the connection to the original visualization.

5. Accessibility and impact

Accessibility is a central motivation behind this project. Earth Jukebox aims to give blind and low-vision users another way to experience Earth science information. It also creates an engaging learning experience for students, educators and the general public.

By combining visual exploration with sound, we hope to make environmental information more inclusive and memorable.

6. Future possibilities

Future development could include direct integration with NASA scientific datasets, more advanced data-driven sonification, additional instruments and sound profiles, improved screen-reader support, and testing with blind and low-vision users.

Our goal is simple: make the story of our changing planet something everyone can experience.
